Every mammal has a four-chambered heart..why: Stated explicitly (88 + 35 exact sentences in two wordings, 1,813 co-occurrences) and in Wikipedia's Mammal article. A plain class rule, held directly (very_unlikely to be derived); no subclass chain gives it.

sources.note: Approximate. Weak by-name storage for dolphins: sampled hits include a FAQ asking how many chambers dolphins' hearts have, and mammal feature lists.

sources.quote: The mammalian heart has four chambers, two upper atria, the receiving chambers, and two lower ventricles, the discharging chambers.

Every bird has feathers..why: Feathers are the first trait Wikipedia's article gives for the class.

sources.quote: Birds are vertebrate animals constituting the class Aves, characterised by feathers, toothless beaked jaws, the laying of hard-shelled eggs

The kipunji has a four-chambered heart..why: A monkey described in 2005, known for its discovery and rarity; its heart is never described by name, so only the class rule gives the answer.

sources.note: AND query; the name (1,978) is rare enough that the zero is not a sampling artefact.

The lesula has a four-chambered heart..why: A monkey described in 2012; text about it is about its discovery and its face, never its heart.

sources.note: AND query on the scientific name (276 hits alone).

The olinguito has a four-chambered heart.why: A raccoon-family mammal classified as a species in 2013; widely reported as a discovery, but its heart is never described by name.

sources.note: AND query; the name (5,237) is not frequent enough to be sampled.

The kipunji is a mammal..why: Stated in the prompt; backed by the first sentence of its article (a monkey is a mammal).

Snakes are mammals..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited rule: snakes are reptiles.

notes: TBox contraction paired with biology-replace-0007: removes its original rule (every mammal has a four-chambered heart). Own questions expect 'does not know'; the propositional questions follow strong Kleene logic (all three unknown). Derived: the revision's three inheritance questions, each stating a little-known member's membership in the prompt, so the removed rule is the only route to the answer (two species by name and an application, a labelled heart diagram). Unrelated near: a fish's heart chambers (two) (contraction is exempt from Rule 7). Known weakness: a model that knows the species is a primate or procyonid may reach four through a lower class. Well-known mammals are not asked because their heart may be stored by name.
